digest: The last 24 hours stayed on course. All 32 merges serve charter goals. The 8 diffs I read do what their titles say, add no dependencies and weaken no tests, and a copy of the repo passes 309 tests offline. The day's work built the commute model, HAFAS client, engine, web pages, scheduler, Telegram and ntfy channels, deploy files and legal pages. Late-day merges were small usability and accessibility changes, which count as allowed idle work. The biggest news is two human commits by Tim this morning. They added six real recorded disruption fixtures and fixed three engine bugs that real data exposed, so G1's definition of done now looks largely met. They also show the system misread the recording failures: the API was down and a fake stop id was used, not a sandbox block. Parked recording tasks should be re-checked, and T-0018 revived or closed. The README still says all engine fixtures are synthetic. Costs are high: $64, 119 sandbox denials, and one retry lost to an overly literal gate rule. The repo has no GitHub remote, so the CI and image publishing part of G4 has never run. No pause needed.
